doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: The ECM sound: space, straight eighths, little blues
summary: Discussion of ECM and the typically Scandinavian style: quiet, clean, classical-influenced, seldom bluesy.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What was the — I’m trying to remember the European label that recorded American musicians as well as European musicians.

Keith Jarrett is the principal. And many international — I mean they have a very special sound. I mean among the musicians you could talk about the ECM style, typically European. I wouldn’t say Keith Jarrett is too much into that but well he had a European group, as you know. But the ECM sound is typically Scandinavian and European.
Is it possible to put that into words? Is it less bluesy?

Yes. Definitely less bluesy. I think affected by the classical music, there’s a lot of space, and it’s often quite quiet. It’s very clean in sound, a very good sound. Quite a lot of even eighths. Straight eighths. Not too much, as you say, they very seldom play blues.
Yeah. Well it’s like well we’ve got five minutes left on the session, let’s do a blues. It’s less likely to happen.
